notes: Public NIH and WHO pages only, fetched 2026-11-07. A stated range copies the page's own sentence; no number is derived, converted or interpolated (AM-1).
WHO states weekly activity amounts; the exercise and step concepts record single entries, so no range is taken from it.
AHA and CDC pages refuse automated fetches, so they are not cited.

sources.title: Vital signs
sources.publisher: MedlinePlus, U.S. National Library of Medicine
sources.supports: Pulse, blood pressure, breathing rate and body temperature are the routine vital signs, and each can be measured at home.

stated_ranges.statement: Blood pressure: between 90/60 mmHg and 120/80 mmHg
Blood pressure: between 90/60 mmHg and 120/80 mmHg

sources.title: High Blood Pressure
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)
sources.supports: Blood pressure is written as two numbers, systolic over diastolic, and it changes through the day with activity.

sources.title: Calculate Your BMI
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)
sources.supports: Body mass index is calculated from height and weight; it does not account for muscle mass or bone density.

sources.title: How Much Sleep Is Enough?
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)
sources.supports: Sleep duration is tracked because how long a person sleeps each night is part of everyday health.

stated_ranges.statement: Experts recommend that adults sleep between 7 and 9 hours a night.

sources.title: Physical activity (fact sheet)
sources.supports: Steps and exercise time are simple records of physical activity, which WHO describes as part of health at every age.
